author: blackparadox

judgment.rationale: The report is deterministic and current code identifies a narrow persistence-versus-reconstruction boundary.
evidence: The admin command's pin state persists even though no dock item renders.
The non-admin sibling from the same provider renders correctly.
judgment.recommended_action: Design nested command lookup/reconstruction coverage for dock pins, including elevated PowerToys commands.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers this nested admin command pin.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette records the nested 'Open Hosts File Editor (Admin)' command as pinned, but the dock cannot render it; the non-admin sibling pins normally.
known_information: Both Hosts commands expose Pin to dock, and the admin command changes to Unpin after selection.
The missing dock item still launches correctly from search and prompts for UAC.
Current extension code gives the admin command a stable ID distinct from the non-admin command.
inferences: Persistence succeeds, but dock reconstruction likely fails to resolve the nested admin command back through its provider or wraps it differently from a top-level dock band.
issue_context.analysis: The asymmetry between two commands from the same module rules out Hosts enablement and UAC launch logic. Current dock code persists provider/command IDs and reconstructs pinned items through provider lookup, making nested-command resolution the focused design surface.
initial_investigation: HostsModuleCommandProvider emits com.microsoft.powertoys.hosts.open and com.microsoft.powertoys.hosts.openAdmin as sibling ListItems.
TopLevelCommandManager routes pin-to-dock operations through CommandProviderWrapper using provider and command IDs.
No pull request referencing issue 48254 was found.

actions.label: Design fix
actions.note: Start the bounded fork-side design workflow. This draft performs no upstream write.

actions.label: B
actions.note: Local maintainer verification only; no GitHub write is performed.

proposed_fixes.title: Resolve nested PowerToys commands when rebuilding dock pins
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The dock saves the nested admin command ID, but its rebuild path likely resolves only top-level commands or dock bands and therefore cannot materialize the persisted Hosts admin ListItem.
plan: Trace the provider/command ID written for both Hosts commands and the lookup used during dock rebuild.
Add a provider API path that resolves persisted nested ICommandItems by stable ID without invoking them.
Use the same resolved item wrapper for admin and non-admin commands and remove stale pins only when the provider definitively no longer exposes the ID.
verification: Pin both Hosts commands, restart Command Palette, verify both render, and invoke the admin item to confirm UAC still occurs.

confidence.rationale: The saved-but-invisible state strongly indicates reconstruction failure, but a settings snapshot is needed to confirm the exact provider ID stored.
